title: Cosine similarity - Wikipedia
content: Cosine similarity is a measure of similarity between two non-zero vectors defined in an inner product space. Cosine similarity is the cosine of the angle between the vectors; that is, it is the dot product of the vectors divided by the product of their lengths. A reference guide for high-dimensional information retrieval.
ground_truth_rationale: Timeless mathematical and conceptual reference guide without personal action items.

title: Resource: Metric Selection in High-Dimensional Vector Search
content:
# Resource: Metric Selection in High-Dimensional Vector Search
Technical cheatsheet and syntax reference for distance metrics:
- Cosine Similarity: Measures angle between vectors; invariant to vector magnitude.
- Dot Product: Equal to cosine similarity when vectors are L2-normalized.
- Euclidean (L2) Distance: Measures geometric distance; sensitive to length without normalization.
ground_truth_rationale: Technical cheatsheet and lookup reference documentation for vector search metrics.

title: Archive: Streamlit Second Brain Prototype (Deprecated)

# Archive: Streamlit Second Brain Prototype (Deprecated)
Decision: Abandoned in favor of Jamstack + Vercel Serverless.
Reasons for deprecation:
- Streamlit requires persistent long-running Python containers with stateful WebSockets.
- Canvas reruns entire script on every user click, making graph traversal sluggish.
- Retired and archived in Q1 2026.
ground_truth_rationale: Superseded technical architecture marked deprecated, abandoned, and retired.
